records.text: White now has a passed pawn. Passed, not unstoppable.
Black now has a passed pawn. Passed, not unstoppable.
The better move would have given White a passer. Worth including in the calculation.
The better move would have given Black a passer. Worth including in the calculation.
White has an isolated pawn now. No friendly pawns on the adjacent files. Pieces may still help.
Black has an isolated pawn now. No friendly pawns on the adjacent files. Pieces may still help.
The stronger alternative would have isolated a pawn for White. Better moves can have untidy details.
The stronger alternative would have isolated a pawn for Black. Better moves can have untidy details.
Doubled pawns for White. Same file; no automatic disaster attached.
Doubled pawns for Black. Same file; no automatic disaster attached.
White's pawns would have shared a file after the better move. Doubled does not settle the argument.
Black's pawns would have shared a file after the better move. Doubled does not settle the argument.
White's rook is on an open file now. No pawns. That is the definition, not a promise.
Black's rook is on an open file now. No pawns. That is the definition, not a promise.
The better move would have put White's rook on a file without pawns. Open, not necessarily vacant.
The better move would have put Black's rook on a file without pawns. Open, not necessarily vacant.
Half-open file for White's rook. Enemy pawns remain there; friendly pawns do not.
Half-open file for Black's rook. Enemy pawns remain there; friendly pawns do not.
White's rook would have had a half-open file with the better move. Enemy pawns only; not an empty file.
Black's rook would have had a half-open file with the better move. Enemy pawns only; not an empty file.
White's knight has a defender now. Previously, it had none. Useful distinction.
Black's knight has a defender now. Previously, it had none. Useful distinction.
White's bishop has acquired a guard. It had none before.
Black's bishop has acquired a guard. It had none before.
White's rook is defended after standing loose. Protection has arrived.
Black's rook is defended after standing loose. Protection has arrived.
White's queen is no longer unguarded. Royalty is not a substitute for support.
Black's queen is no longer unguarded. Royalty is not a substitute for support.
The better move would have guarded White's loose knight. Support was available.
The better move would have guarded Black's loose knight. Support was available.
White's bishop would have gained its missing defender with the stronger alternative. A guard was an option.
Black's bishop would have gained its missing defender with the stronger alternative. A guard was an option.
A guard for White's rook, had the better move been played. It lacked one before.
A guard for Black's rook, had the better move been played. It lacked one before.
The stronger choice would have defended White's unguarded queen. Worth including in the comparison.
The stronger choice would have defended Black's unguarded queen. Worth including in the comparison.
White's knight has lost its last guard. Loose now. Not necessarily lost.
Black's knight has lost its last guard. Loose now. Not necessarily lost.
No defenders remain for White's bishop. Its protection has gone; a capture still needs checking.
No defenders remain for Black's bishop. Its protection has gone; a capture still needs checking.
White's rook has lost all its support. Undefended is the fact. Anything further needs evidence.
Black's rook has lost all its support. Undefended is the fact. Anything further needs evidence.
White's queen has lost its last defender. Impressive range, absent cover.
Black's queen has lost its last defender. Impressive range, absent cover.
The better move would have left White's knight without a guard. Strength is judged on more than that.
The better move would have left Black's knight without a guard. Strength is judged on more than that.
White's bishop would have lost its remaining protection after the stronger move. That alone would not prove a loss.
Black's bishop would have lost its remaining protection after the stronger move. That alone would not prove a loss.
The stronger alternative would have left White's rook undefended. Count the missing guard, not imaginary winnings.
The stronger alternative would have left Black's rook undefended. Count the missing guard, not imaginary winnings.
White's queen would have lost its last guard with the better move. Even the better choice has details to count.
Black's queen would have lost its last guard with the better move. Even the better choice has details to count.
The knight leaves its starting square for the first time. Placement is the next question.
First deployment for this knight. The original square is vacated.
A knight comes out from home. Its development begins; the position gets the final vote.
The knight makes its first move. No longer on its original square.
The bishop leaves home for the first time. A start, literally.
Initial deployment of the bishop. It has vacated its starting square.
A bishop comes off its original square. That is development; quality is another question.
First departure for this bishop. The starting square is behind it.
The better move would have started a knight's development. A first departure worth examining.
A knight would have left home for the first time with the stronger alternative.
The stronger choice would have moved an undeveloped knight off its original square. Different deployment.
A knight would have begun its development with the better move. Inspect the destination.
The better alternative would have taken a bishop off its starting square for the first time.
A bishop's initial departure was available with the stronger choice. Check the proposed placement.
The stronger move would have begun a bishop's development. It would have left the starting square behind.
An undeveloped bishop would have left home under the better choice. Development is the starting point for judging that move.
A worse position than the better move offered. That difference is the cost.
The stronger choice gives a better position. This move falls short.
Less than was available. Put the stronger move beside this one; the comparison matters.
The position pays for this choice relative to the best move. The difference warrants attention.
An immediate capture is available to the other side. Profit still requires calculation.
The opponent can capture on the next move. Available does not mean free.
A capture can come straight back. Include it in the arithmetic.
The reply may take something immediately. Check the result before celebrating it.
You punished the last error. The opponent supplied it; you used it.
That makes use of the opponent's mistake. A chance properly collected.
The previous error costs the opponent now. You did not let it pass.
Another move was stronger. It deserves the comparison.
There is a better alternative to put beside this choice.
The move not played offered more. Compare that option.
The passed pawn moves nearer promotion. Nearer is not there.
A passer advances. Less distance remains; that does not remove the opposition.
The strongest reply checks the king. That takes precedence.
Best reply: check. Resolve the king's problem first.
The intended lesson move. Done correctly.
That is what this lesson called for. Continue.
Correct execution of the lesson's move. Nothing to amend.
Correct move. More puzzle remains.
That answer stands. Find the next part.
Right, but not finished. Continue solving.
Matches the opening repertoire. Accepted.
The studied opening answer. Recalled correctly.
That is the move in the material. No correction needed.
Best. The right choice needs little decoration.
The strongest move available. Adequate grounds for approval.
Sound, though something stronger exists. Good, then.
A good move, short of best. No drama required.
